biggest_catch: LessonFace's official pages quote average prices paid per lesson, but no concrete guaranteed worker pay and no official payout schedule for teachers.
catches: No official concrete worker pay: official figures are category averages (e.g. $29.98 classical piano, $38.31 opera per lesson), not guaranteed earnings.
No official payout schedule for teachers found in LessonFace's official pages (weekly-Friday payouts are a third-party claim).
Commission and teacher-side fees are not published on official pages.
Marketplace reality: earnings depend on attracting students at your own rates.

c1.evidence: LessonFace official pages state teachers set their own rates and publish category averages (e.g. $29.98-$41.30 per lesson) - not a concrete worker pay figure.

c2.evidence: Official pages state only that 'teachers receive their payment after the lesson has been completed' - no concrete payout schedule.

c3.evidence: Registering as a teacher is free; no upfront fee documented.

c4.evidence: Fails both the official-pay and official-timing requirements.

eligibility: Apply as a teacher; set your own lesson rates and availability.
maximize: LessonFace is rejected here because its official pages publish average lesson prices but no concrete worker pay and no teacher payout schedule. If official terms ever publish them, note the official mechanics: you set your own rates (LessonFace displays category averages on its site), lessons are usually 30-60 minutes, and teachers receive payment after each lesson is completed.
notes: LessonFace is a real music-lesson marketplace, but official pages quote average prices paid by students, not guaranteed teacher pay, and publish no teacher payout schedule.
